newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gnome-snatchers strike in French gardens.
newsitem.headline: Gnome-snatchers strike in French gardens.

text.p: French garden gnomes are mysteriously disappearing from their peaceful homes to start a new life in the forests.
Masked commandos of the Garden Gnomes' Liberation Front (FLNJ) have been kidnapping the small cheerful-looking statues during night raids and "freeing" them in the woods.

"Each group of commandos comprises seven members in reference to Snow White's Seven Dwarves," said Jean-Marc Seigner, a journalist who met the kidnappers. "They pretend Snow White is the driving force behind their gang."

"They called me to claim several kidnappings," said Seigner, who works for a local weekly in the Normandy town of Alencon. "They asked me to go to some remote place in a nearby forest and there they were, with masks on their faces and lots of gnomes standing around them in the snow."
Paramilitary gendarmes, who have received several complaints about the gnome abductors, are seeking to find the thieves.
Seigner said the first group of commandos was created in Alencon but two others existed in Rennes and Caen.

"The one in Alencon renamed themselves FLNJ-Historic Wing to make it clear that they started it," he said. "A meeting between the three branches is expected to take place in the next few days in a secret place near Alencon."
The abductors are modelling themselves on separatist guerrillas on the Mediterranean island of Corsica -- the most radical group of which is the FLNC-Historic Wing.
The FLNJ members repaint the gnomes in ugly colours to make sure that their owners would not recognize them and take them back if they spotted them in the countryside.
A cold snap in France complicates life for the kidnappers as the gnomes are often taken inside to stay warm and prevent cracking. But otherwise, they say it is fairly easy to abduct a gnome.
"Dogs are not a problem," Seigner explained. "People who have gnomes usually don't have a dog because it would wee on them."
Seigner said he did not know the reasons for the kidnappings. "All I can say is that the gnomes I saw in the forest looked happy enough," he said.
